descriptionChirho: Spirit in the Aramaic portions of Daniel, referring to either the divine spirit indwelling a person or the human spirit as the seat of inner life. Used of Daniel possessing 'the spirit of the holy gods' (Dan 4:8, 4:9, 4:18, 5:11, 5:14), of an 'excellent spirit' in Daniel (Dan 6:3), of Daniel's own spirit being troubled (Dan 7:15), and of Nebuchadnezzar's spirit becoming hardened in pride (Dan 5:20). Arabic رُوحُ/رُوحِي (spirit/my spirit), Korean 영 (spirit), Spanish espíritu, Hindi आत्मा (soul/spirit), German Geist, French esprit. Cross-linguistically uniform: all languages use their primary term for 'spirit/soul' rather than 'wind,' confirming the immaterial/spiritual sense throughout these passages.

Wind as a natural meteorological phenomenon in Aramaic Daniel. In Dan 7:2, the 'four winds of heaven' (רוּחֵי שְׁמַיָּא) churn the great sea in Daniel's vision; in Dan 2:35, the wind (רוּחָא) carries away the chaff of the shattered image. Arabic رِيَاحِ/الرِّيحُ (winds/the wind), Korean 바람들이/바람이 (winds/the wind), Spanish vientos/el viento (winds/the wind), Hindi पवनें/हवा (breezes/air). The cross-linguistic evidence decisively separates this from the 'spirit' sense: Arabic uses رِيَاح (winds) rather than رُوح (spirit), Korean uses 바람 (wind) rather than 영 (spirit), and Hindi uses पवन/हवा (wind/air) rather than आत्मा (soul).
